<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} = 2</annotation></semantics></math> is a rate per unit of time, not the slope; the slope divides by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is 0 here.

Length is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_a^b \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(t) = 1 - \cos t</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(t) = \sin t</annotation></semantics></math>, over the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-interval that traces the arch once.

On <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(\frac{t}{2}\right) \ge 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the integrand is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{4\sin^2\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\sin\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>. Distance along the path uses the speed <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{(x')^2 + (y')^2}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'</annotation></semantics></math> alone.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 3 + \frac{4 + 6}{2}(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 13</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx -1 + \frac{1 + (-2)}{2}(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -2</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: These are the changes in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>; add the starting point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, -1)</annotation></semantics></math>.
This subtracts the starting point from the changes; the start is added.
Right: start plus the trapezoid approximation of each change.

This uses the left-end rates only, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4(2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1(2)</annotation></semantics></math>; a trapezoid averages both ends.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(t) = \left\langle 2t, -3t^2 \right\rangle + \mathbf{C}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(0) = \mathbf{C} = \left\langle 1, 3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(t) = \left\langle 2t + 1, 3 - 3t^2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: This antiderivative has <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(0) = \left\langle 0, 0 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>; add the constant vector <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 1, 3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> so that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(0)</annotation></semantics></math> matches.

The initial velocity is added, not subtracted: at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> this gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle -1, -3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>.

The antiderivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-6t</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3t^2</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-6t</annotation></semantics></math>.

Right: antidifferentiate each component and match <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(0)</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(t) = 3 - 3t^2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(t) = 3t - t^3 + C</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 4</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C = 4</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(t) = 4 + 3t - t^3</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(t) = t^2 + t</annotation></semantics></math> (since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(0) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>) and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(t) = 4 + 3t - t^3</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 4 + 2, 4 + 6 - 8 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left\langle 6, 2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: both initial conditions are used.

This antidifferentiates twice with both constants left out; use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(0)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(0)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(2) = \left\langle 5, -9 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, not the position.

The vertical component needs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 4</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 + 6 - 8 = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(t) = 3 - 3t^2</annotation></semantics></math> is positive for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t < 1</annotation></semantics></math> and negative for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t > 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> increases and then decreases: its greatest value is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(1) = 4 + 3 - 1 = 6</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(0)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^t 6s^2\,ds</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 2t^3</annotation></semantics></math>. (Likewise <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(t) = 2 + \sin t</annotation></semantics></math>.)

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mi>π</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^t \pi\cos(\pi s)\,ds</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \sin(\pi t)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 3 + 1 = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

Antidifferentiate each component: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int e^{2t}\,dt = \frac{1}{2}e^{2t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{t}\,dt = \ln|t|</annotation></semantics></math>. The constant is a vector <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{C} = \left\langle C_1, C_2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, one constant per component.
options: These are derivatives of the components; the integral reverses differentiation.
Right: one antiderivative per component, plus a constant vector.

Differentiating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{2t}</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2e^{2t}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the antiderivative needs the factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{t^2}</annotation></semantics></math> is the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{t}</annotation></semantics></math>; its antiderivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|t|</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Integrate each component: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 3t^2\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 (4t^3 + 1)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (t^4 + t)\Big|_0^1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: These are the derivatives at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>; integrate instead.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(4) = 1 + \ln 5 > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing (right); <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(4)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3\cos 4</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.961</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx -1.961 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing (down).

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1 + \ln(t + 1) > 0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \ge 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the particle moves right.

Right: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x' > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y' < 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Distance <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_0^4 \sqrt{(1 + \ln(t + 1))^2 + (3\cos t)^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>11.922</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 11.922</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(t) = \left\langle 2t, 3t^2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(1) = \left\langle 2, 3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> and the speed is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>13</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{4 + 9} = \sqrt{13}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, the slope of the path. Speed is the magnitude of the velocity.

That adds the components <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 + 3</annotation></semantics></math>; use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2^2 + 3^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the length of the position <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 1, 1 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>; speed uses the velocity.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} = 12 - 3t^2 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, that is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t > 2</annotation></semantics></math>: the interval <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 < t < 4</annotation></semantics></math>. The sign of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> does not decide this.
options: On <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < t < 2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing (<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x' = 2t - 4 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>) but <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y' = 12 - 3t^2 > 0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> increases.

Right: read the sign of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

This reads <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{12 - 3t^2}{2t - 4}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is negative on both intervals. That says the path falls as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> increases, not that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> decreases in time.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} = 12 - 3t^2</annotation></semantics></math> is negative for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 < t < 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(t) = \left\langle -3\sin t, 3\cos t \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, so the speed is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{9(\sin^2 t + \cos^2 t)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3</annotation></semantics></math>. Distance <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_0^{2\pi} 3\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 6\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, one trip around a circle of radius 3.

Speed <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sqrt{9t^4 + 9t^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3t\sqrt{t^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \ge 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Distance <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></msubsup><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_0^{\sqrt{3}} 3t\sqrt{t^2 + 1}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>0</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (t^2 + 1)^{3/2}\Big|_0^{\sqrt{3}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 8 - 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 7</annotation></semantics></math>.

A collision needs the same point at the same time. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2t = t + 2</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, and then <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^2 - 1 = 3 = 3t - 3</annotation></semantics></math>. Both are at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 3)</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: both coordinates match at the same time.

The paths do cross at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(8, 15)</annotation></semantics></math>, but A is there at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math> and B at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math>: different times, no collision.

At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinates match but the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinates are 2 and 3.

They do collide: at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> both <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> agree.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = f(\theta)\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, so by the product rule <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= f'(\theta)\cos\theta + f(\theta)(-\sin\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: product rule on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = f(\theta)\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

The distance from the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|x| = |r\cos\theta|</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(2.5)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2.5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2.5 + 2\cos 2.5</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>0.898</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0.898</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2.5</mn><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.719</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = r\cos 2.5 \approx -0.719</annotation></semantics></math>, so the distance is about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.719</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.719</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></msubsup><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}\int_{\alpha}^{\beta} r^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2 = 9\sin^2(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>; the petal is traced once as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> runs from 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is missing: each thin sector has area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2\,\Delta\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, like a slice of a circle.

Right: one half, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> squared, and the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>-limits where the petal starts and ends at the pole.

Square all of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3\sin(2\theta))^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 9\sin^2(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>, so the 3 is squared too.

From 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> the curve traces two petals; the shaded petal ends at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> returns to 0.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2} 9\sin^2(2\theta)\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{9}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{1 - \cos(4\theta)}{2}\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{9}{4}\left[\theta - \frac{\sin(4\theta)}{4}\right]_0^{\pi/2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{9}{4} \cdot \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{9\pi}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The four petals have equal area, so the total is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 \cdot \frac{9\pi}{8} = \frac{9\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Equivalently, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{2\pi} 9\sin^2(2\theta)\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{9\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> goes once around, each petal is traced exactly once.

Solve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\sin(2\theta) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0, \frac{\pi}{2}, \pi, \ldots</annotation></semantics></math> Between <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and the curve leaves the pole and returns to it once: one petal.
options: True here, but it is a coincidence of this rose. Limits come from where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 0</annotation></semantics></math> or curves meet, found from the equation.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 3\sin\pi = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; the tip, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, is at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Right: between two consecutive zeros of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, the curve traces one petal.

The period of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, which would give limits 0 and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>: two petals.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msubsup><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/4} 9\sin^2(2\theta)\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{9}{4}\left[\theta - \frac{\sin(4\theta)}{4}\right]_0^{\pi/4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>16</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{9\pi}{16}</annotation></semantics></math>, half the petal: the line <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> through the tip splits it into mirror halves.

The circle is traced once for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le \pi</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mn>16</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi} 16\sin^2\theta\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 8 \cdot \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, the area of a circle of radius 2.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{2\pi} (1 - \sin\theta)^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}\int_0^{2\pi} \left(1 - 2\sin\theta + \frac{1 - \cos(2\theta)}{2}\right)d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}\left(2\pi - 0 + \pi\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{3\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + 2\cos\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Between them <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, and the curve traces the inner loop once; squaring <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> makes the integrand positive. The area is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi - \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: From 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> the curve traces the upper half of the big outer loop.
That is the whole outer loop, where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r > 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

Right: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r < 0</annotation></semantics></math> between the two zeros <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, and that stretch traces the inner loop.
A full turn counts the inner loop inside the outer one a second time.

A slice of a circle of radius <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> with angle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is the fraction <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\Delta\theta}{2\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> of the disk, so its area is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\Delta\theta}{2\pi}\pi r^2 = \frac{1}{2}r^2\,\Delta\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. Adding slices and taking the limit gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></msubsup><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{\alpha}^{\beta} r^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: the polar area integral is the limit of these sectors' areas added up.

Polar regions are cut into wedges, not rectangles; a wedge's area grows with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2</annotation></semantics></math> is not an average; it is the slice area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\Delta\theta}{2\pi} \cdot \pi r^2</annotation></semantics></math> per unit of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

Some curves are traced twice over <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 2\pi]</annotation></semantics></math>, which is a reason to change the limits, not the source of the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msubsup><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/3} 2^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, one sixth of the disk's area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mi>θ</mi></msqrt><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{2\pi} (\sqrt{\theta})^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}\int_0^{2\pi} \theta\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{(2\pi)^2}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \pi^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Each width is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2.5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3.2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{6}\left(2^2 + 2.5^2 + 3.2^2\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>20.49</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\pi}{12}(20.49)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>5.364</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 5.364</annotation></semantics></math>.

The trapezoidal sum averages the left and right sums: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2.5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>3.2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{6} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\left(2^2 + 2(2.5^2) + 2(3.2^2) + 3^2\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>22.99</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\pi}{12}(22.99)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>6.019</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 6.019</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></msubsup><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{\alpha}^{\beta} r^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is the area of the region bounded by the polar curve and the rays <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \alpha</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \beta</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: The length of a curve uses a different integral (arc length); this one adds wedge areas.

The region is bounded by two rays from the pole, not by vertical lines at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-values.

An average would divide <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>r</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int r\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math> by the interval's length; this adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

Right: the region swept by the radius as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> goes from 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: The integrand is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2</annotation></semantics></math>, so a left sum is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2.5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{6}\left(\frac{1}{2}(2)^2 + \frac{1}{2}(2.5)^2 + \frac{1}{2}(3.2)^2\right)</annotation></semantics></math>. The student's sum adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>-values as if the region were made of rectangles.

That would be a right sum instead of a left sum, still missing the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and the squares.

Right: each wedge is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2\,\Delta\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, so the sum is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>2.5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3.2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{12}(2^2 + 2.5^2 + 3.2^2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

It does, with a Riemann sum of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2</annotation></semantics></math>, as for any definite integral.

Setting <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\sin\theta = 2</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

There <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 4\sin\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math>: the pole, which is not on the circle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 4</annotation></semantics></math> on one circle and 2 on the other; they do not meet there.

why.correct: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>β</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}\int_{\alpha}^{\beta} \left(R^2 - r^2\right)d\theta</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R = 4\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> (outer) and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math> (inner), from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: outer radius squared minus inner radius squared, between the crossing angles.

Square each radius separately: the region is a big wedge minus a small wedge, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}(R^2 - r^2)</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}(R - r)^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>R</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R - r)^2 = R^2 - 2Rr + r^2</annotation></semantics></math>, which is not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^2 - r^2</annotation></semantics></math>.
